title: Categorical patterns and their fibered objects (fully scaled quasicategory case)
statement:
Fix nested universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Use its simplicial sets, quasicategories, coherent diagrams and limits; inner fibrations and cocartesian edges from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]; marked simplicial sets and marking-preserving maps from [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]; simplicial joins, left cones and relative limit diagrams from [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]; and classifying functors of cocartesian fibrations from [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Simplicial sets defining a pattern or an object over it are $\mathcal U$-small; $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ is the infinity category of $\mathcal U$-small quasicategories, formed in $\mathcal U'$.

A categorical pattern here is a triple $\mathfrak P=(C,S,\{p_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A})$, where $C$ is a small quasicategory, $S\subseteq C_1$ contains every degenerate edge, $A$ is a small set, and $p_\alpha:K_\alpha^{\triangleleft}\to C$ is a simplicial map for each $\alpha\in A$, with $K_\alpha$ a small quasicategory and every edge of $K_\alpha^{\triangleleft}$ mapping into $S$. The left cone is $K^{\triangleleft}=\Delta^0\star K$, with new initial vertex $*$. All $2$-simplices of $C$ are scaled. Write $\bar C=(C,S)$ and $\mathsf M_{\mathfrak P}=\mathrm{sSet}^+_{/\bar C}$. An object is a marked simplicial set $(X,T)$ with a marking-preserving map $q:(X,T)\to(C,S)$; a morphism is a simplicial map over $C$ preserving marked edges, with the usual identities and composition.

Such an object is $\mathfrak P$-fibered when all four conditions hold:
(i) $q:X\to C$ is an inner fibration.
(ii) For each edge $a:c\to d$ in $S$ and vertex $x\in X_c$, there is a $q$-cocartesian edge with source $x$ over $a$; $T$ is exactly the set of $q$-cocartesian edges whose images lie in $S$.
(iii) For every $\alpha\in A$, put $X_\alpha=X\times_C K_\alpha^{\triangleleft}$, formed degreewise, and let $q_\alpha:X_\alpha\to K_\alpha^{\triangleleft}$ be its projection. This is required to be a cocartesian fibration whose classifying functor $K_\alpha^{\triangleleft}\to\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ is a limit diagram, that is, a $p$-limit diagram in the sense of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] for the unique functor $p:\mathrm{Cat}_\infty\to\Delta^0$. Here classifying functor has the meaning in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], so its values are the fibers and its arrows are cocartesian transport.
(iv) For every $\alpha\in A$ and every cocartesian section $s:K_\alpha^{\triangleleft}\to X_\alpha$ of $q_\alpha$, its composite $\bar s:K_\alpha^{\triangleleft}\to X$ is a $q$-limit diagram in the sense of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. A cocartesian section means $q_\alpha s=\mathrm{id}$ and $s$ carries every edge to a $q_\alpha$-cocartesian edge.

Empty $A$ and empty $K_\alpha$ are permitted. An empty limit means a terminal object; it is not omitted from conditions (iii) and (iv).
